subject.title: Context pruning mode 'off' not preventing compactions (Anthropic API key, cache-ttl smart defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw support a hard-limit-only or fully-off automatic compaction mode, and should persisted compaction entries carry a closed trigger reason?
rationale: Current main already honors pruning off, but the remaining request changes compaction safety semantics and transcript metadata, which needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Define hard-limit semantics
options.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep current compaction policy
options.body: Treat automatic compaction as always enabled by design and narrow follow-up work to verified false low-context triggers and clearer docs.

options.title: Wait for live Anthropic proof
options.body: Require a current-main Anthropic API-key reproduction before accepting new compaction semantics beyond the related low-context compaction reports.

recommendation.title: Define hard-limit semantics
recommendation.body: Add an approved config contract that preserves overflow recovery while disabling threshold/safeguard compaction, plus trigger metadata, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent compaction reserve and runtime ownership history makes this the closest routing owner for the config/safety decision.
